recommendedTitle: Legacy flat PATCH /api/contacts authorizes on membership alone, so a `caller` can rewrite any contact in its workspace and clear the opt_out consent flag the…
summary: The legacy flat contact route under app/routes/api+ authorizes POST and PATCH /api/contacts on workspace MEMBERSHIP alone: the body workspace_id is taken from the request, requireWorkspaceAccess is called with no minRole, and no product…
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. `PATCH /api/contacts` requires the `campaigns.write` capability, so a workspace `caller` cannot rewrite contacts through it, and the write accepts only the fields the contact editor exposes — `opt_out`, `created_by`, `workspace` and `id` are unreachable. Creating a contact stays membership-only, because callers create contacts from the chat composer and the queue picker.
rootCause: app/routes/api+/contacts.action.server.ts performs the authorization decision with a bare membership check (requireWorkspaceAccess({ user, workspaceId }) at line 41) and never calls a capability or role guard, while the canonical contact create/update route gates the same state change on the `member` role (app/routes/workspaces+/$id/contacts/$contactId.action.server.ts:37). The legacy route then hands the whole request body to updateContact, which uses it verbatim as the UPDATE column set (app/lib/database/contact.server.ts:266), so a column the product deliberately excludes from its own editor - opt_out, the consent flag - becomes caller-controlled.
resolution: Fixed in #2986: the `requireFlatApiCapability` gate on the PATCH branch (`app/routes/api+/contacts.action.server.ts`), the `CONTACT_UPDATE_FIELDS` allowlist in `updateContact` (`app/lib/database/contact.server.ts`), and the capability declared in `scripts/capability-baseline.json`.
acceptanceCriteria: A workspace member holding the lowest role (`caller`) must not be able to mutate an existing contact record, and no role may set the opt_out consent flag through the generic contact-update endpoint. The product already enforces both rules on its canonical contact editor route: the write action requires the `member` role and answers 403 to a `caller` (app/routes/workspaces+/$id/contacts/$contactId.action.server.ts:37), and it writes a fixed field set that excludes opt_out (app/server/contact-editor.server.ts:8). Contact deletion is `campaigns.write` plus a `member` floor (app/routes/api+/contacts/$contactId.action.server.ts:24), and `caller` does not hold campaigns.write (app/lib/capabilities.ts:76). The legacy flat route should apply the same capability and role floor to PATCH /api/contacts and accept a fixed column set rather than the raw request body. Contact CREATION via POST /api/contacts must stay membership-only, because the chat composer and the queue picker legitimately create contacts as a `caller` (app/routes/api+/contacts.loader.server.ts:33).

resolution: Fixed in #2925 (`b5a4dc18`): the tenant predicate is a property of the helper, not an optional argument. `app/lib/campaign-queue-db.server.ts:235` (by-id dequeue), `:604` (failed-attempt counter), `app/routes/api+/ivr.action.server.ts:80`.

ADR-0004 (`app/server/tenant-db.ts:32-35`, `app/db/workspace-scoped-tables.ts`) makes `createTenantDb(workspaceId)` the only tenant-data accessor for route code precisely because the base `db` client bypasses tenancy, and the audit's architecture summary names `createTenantDb` as the strongest source-visible control on the tenant-to-tenant boundary with no RLS behind it. The repository already applied exactly this discipline to the plpgsql equivalents in client/migrations/20260807120000_scope_dequeue_and_outreach_attempt_by_workspace.sql, which added a mandatory workspace parameter to `dequeue_contact` and `create_outreach_attempt` and named /api/dial, /api/hangup and /api/questions as the exposed callers. recommendedTitle: POST /account/security intent=enable replaces an already-enrolled second factor with only the password, bypassing the protected-user rule
summary: The two-factor enrolment state machine at POST /account/security has no prior-state check on its `enable` transition and no protected-user check, while the sibling `disable` transition has both
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. `intent=enable` refuses with `Two-factor authentication is already enabled.` when the account is enrolled, so a password alone can no longer replace an existing factor.
rootCause: app/routes/account.security.loader.server.ts:61-100 handles `intent=enable` as a stateless operation: it reads the password from the form and calls Better Auth's enableTwoFactor without checking whether the account already has an enrolled second factor (isTwoFactorEnabled / the auth_two_factor row) and without applying userIsTwoFactorProtected, which the `disable` branch does apply at line 151. Better Auth's enableTwoFactor is a replacement operation (node_modules/better-auth/dist/plugins/two-factor/index.mjs:113 deletes the existing auth_two_factor row and line 126 recreates it with `verified` inherited from the previous verified row), so the missing server-side state check turns an…
resolution: Fixed in #2901 (`69587240`): the enable branch checks `isTwoFactorEnabled(user.id)` before calling Better Auth's `enableTwoFactor`, which replaces the factor. `app/routes/account.security.loader.server.ts`, `app/routes/api+/auth/$.loader.server.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: Replacing or removing an enrolled account's second factor must require assurance beyond the first factor, and a privileged account's 2FA state must be governed by the same rule that already blocks intent=disable. Concretely: the server must reject `intent=enable` when the account already has an enrolled second factor (mirroring the client-side guards at app/routes/account.security.tsx:107 and app/routes/account.tsx:229), and any deliberate re-enrolment must first prove possession of the current factor (the existing TOTP code or a backup code) and must satisfy userIsTwoFactorProtected for privileged accounts, so that the effective policy on both transitions is the same.

recommendedTitle: Platform-admin 'Disable user' writes access_level='disabled', a value no authorization path enforces: the disabled user keeps a live session and full workspace…
summary: The admin panel offers a 'Disable user' control on every user row (POST /admin with _action=toggle_user_status) and the JSON admin plane exposes the same operation (POST /api/admin/dashboard with {"action":"toggle_user_status"}); PATCH…
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. Disabling an account revokes its sessions, and both session-resolution paths treat `access_level = 'disabled'` as unauthenticated, so a disabled account can neither keep using a live cookie or bearer token nor obtain a working session again. Workspace membership is kept, so restoring a level restores access.
rootCause: disableUser treats the string 'disabled' as an account state, but 'disabled' is only a free-text column value on public.user (plain `text DEFAULT 'standard'`, no CHECK constraint, no enum) with no consumer. The disable operation is written as a single-column UPDATE and never revokes the target's Better Auth sessions (auth_session rows) and never touches workspace_member - the two things that actually grant the user authority - so both remain in force. The enforcement that does exist for access_level ('sudo' only) is read in four TypeScript sites and one plpgsql function, none of which is on the disabled path, so the disable control cannot fail closed: it can only fail open. The codebase…
resolution: Fixed in #2978: `disableUser` revokes the account's sessions (`app/lib/platform-admin.server.ts`), `getSession` and `resolveBearerSessionUser` reject a disabled account (`app/lib/auth.server.ts`), and the admin console states what the level means (`admin+/users/$userId/edit.route.tsx`).
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing 'Disable user' in the admin panel, or setting access_level='disabled' through PATCH /api/admin/users/:userId, must stop the target account from acting: its live sessions must stop working, it must not be able to sign in again, and it must no longer be admitted to its workspaces, so an administrator who offboards or contains a user is not told 'User disabled successfully' while the account keeps working.

recommendedTitle: PATCH /api/admin/users/:userId silently rewrites access_level to 'standard' when the field is omitted, stripping sudo (and the 2FA mandate) from the target

summary: The application's rule 'privileged accounts cannot disable two-factor authentication' is implemented in exactly one place - the intent=disable branch of the POST /account/security action…

recommendedTitle: Public contact form writes unescaped caller text into the ops-inbox email HTML body
summary: The public, unauthenticated contact form POST /api/contact-form copies the caller-supplied `name` and `message` form fields into the `html` part of the email sent to the CallCaster operations inbox
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. The public contact form escapes the visitor's name and message in the HTML body of the operations-inbox email, so an anonymous submission cannot inject links, images or markup; the plain-text body still carries their words verbatim.
rootCause:
app/routes/api+/contact-form.action.server.ts builds the outbound email HTML body with a raw template literal (`html: `

From: ${name}.


${message}``) and never routes the two caller-controlled fields through the repository's own `escapeHtml()` helper from app/lib/email-html.ts, which the module does not import.
resolution: Fixed in #2976: `escapeHtml` from `app/lib/email-html.ts` at the sink in `app/routes/api+/contact-form.action.server.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria:
The visitor's `name` and `message` must reach the operations inbox as literal text, not as markup. The sibling outbound emails that carry caller text escape it first, so the contact form should render `

recommendedTitle: Media-stream token without a call SID lets a WebSocket peer overwrite another tenant's coaching rows
summary: The media-stream service authenticates a session with an HMAC token that binds the workspace and only optionally the call
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. A media-stream token cannot be minted without a call SID — `createMediaStreamToken` throws when `callSid` is absent — and the DB writer resolves coaching rows through that call rather than a peer-supplied identity.
rootCause: The call SID is an optional claim in the signed media-stream token, and the service's call-binding check is conditional on that claim being present (`tokenCallSid && msg.start.callSid && msg.start.callSid !== tokenCallSid`). When the token carries no call SID the check is skipped and the row key of the unscoped admin-DB writes is taken from a client-supplied frame field, so the token authorizes writes for a resource it never named. The fix that introduced the check (commit 55e6477b, 'fix(media-stream): bind transcript/coaching writes to the token's callSid (#1530)') hardened only the mint paths that happen to know the call SID at TwiML-generation time and left the predictive auto-dial path…
resolution: Fixed in #2926 (`1cb8dad0`): `app/lib/media-stream-token.server.ts:41` requires the call SID, `app/lib/media-stream-twiml.server.ts` and `app/routes/api+/auto-dial/$roomId.action.server.ts` pass it.
acceptanceCriteria: A media-stream token must authorize writes only for the workspace and the call it was minted for, and a `start` frame that names any other call must be refused. Commit 55e6477b states the intent explicitly: 'A token holder for their own workspace could send another workspace's live Call SID and inject rows the victim later sees as genuine.' For that to hold, every minted token must carry the call SID it authorizes (the field must not be optional), and the stream handler must refuse any `start` frame whose call SID is missing or different from the token's, rather than falling back to the frame's value.

recommendedTitle: Changing the account password leaves every other session of that account usable
summary: PATCH /api/me is the product's only password-change path
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. Changing the account password revokes every other session of the account, including bearer tokens from `POST /api/auth/token`, and returns a replacement session in the body and as a cookie so the caller is not logged out by its own change.
rootCause: app/lib/platform-auth.server.ts:468 invokes auth.api.changePassword without revokeOtherSessions, so the password rotation updates the credential hash and leaves the account's other auth_session rows (and therefore every other session cookie and bearer token) valid; the session invalidation the app performs for the reset path (app/server/auth-instance.ts:30, revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset) has no equivalent on the change path, and no other control in app/ revokes sessions on a password change.
resolution: Fixed in #2979: `changePassword` is called with `revokeOtherSessions: true` and `returnHeaders: true` (`app/lib/platform-auth.server.ts`), and `PATCH /api/me` returns `session_token` (`app/routes/api+/me.action.server.ts`).
acceptanceCriteria: Changing the account password invalidates the account's other sessions, so a password rotation is an effective response to suspected session compromise. The app already states this intent for the sibling path: app/server/auth-instance.ts:28-30 sets revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset with the comment that the sessions which already exist are exactly the ones that must stop working.

recommendedTitle: Workspace SSE stream re-checks membership only, so a demoted owner or a revoked API key keeps the owner-only event stream
summary: GET /api/workspaces/:workspaceId/events is gated at connect time on the owner-only `audit.read` capability (`dataPlaneCapabilityAuth("audit.read")`, events.loader.server.ts:61), but the only periodic re-authorization of the already-open…
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. An open workspace event stream re-applies the authorization that opened it: a session or bearer actor must still hold a valid session and a role whose current capabilities include `audit.read`, and an API-key actor's row must still exist, be unexpired and carry `audit.read` in its current scopes. Either failing closes the stream with `workspace_access_revoked`; a failed lookup still keeps it open.
rootCause: The stream's revocation hook only enforces workspace membership, not the authorization decision that opened the stream. In `app/routes/api+/workspaces+/$workspaceId/events.loader.server.ts`, `stillHasWorkspaceAccess` (line 89) returns `true` unconditionally for API-key actors (`if (!auth.userId) return true;`, line 92) and otherwise evaluates only `getUserRole({ user: { id: auth.userId }, workspaceId }) != null` (line 94) - i.e. "is there still a `workspace_member` row". It never re-derives the actor's capabilities from the current role, never re-reads the API key row (existence/expiry/scopes), and never re-validates the session. The 15s heartbeat (lines 174-186) is the only place a…
resolution: Fixed in #2989: `stillHasWorkspaceAccess` in `app/routes/api+/workspaces+/$workspaceId/events.loader.server.ts` now evaluates the capability through `capabilitySetForRole` / `capabilitySetFromScopeAllowlist` instead of testing membership.
acceptanceCriteria: The stream's own doc comment states that it outlives the connect-time check by design, and its gate is deliberately the owner-only `audit.read` capability - the same capability the sibling `/api/workspaces/:workspaceId/audit-events` endpoint enforces (audit-events.loader.server.ts:7). A stream that outlives its connect check must therefore be re-authorized with the same authority on every tick: re-derive the actor's current capabilities from the CURRENT workspace role and require `audit.read`; for API-key actors re-read the key row and require the current scopes to contain `audit.read`; for cookie actors re-validate the session. When the re-authorization fails the stream must emit `workspace_access_revoked` and close - exactly as it already does today for a removed member.

recommendedTitle: Worker's affected-row count is always zero, so dead-letter and crash-recovery alerts never fire
summary: The worker decides whether a write did anything by counting the rows it affected, but it reads that count from the wrong field of the wrong shape
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. The worker reads the affected-row count from the database driver's `count` before the array length, so a write that changed rows is no longer read as a write that changed nothing. The stale-claim reset signal and the dead-letter and crash-recovery alerts that depend on it fire again.
rootCause: affectedRowCount() in app/lib/worker/poll-jobs.server.ts:79-86 tests Array.isArray(result) before the driver's count property. Under the postgres-js driver the application uses (app/server/db.ts:1,63,72; drizzle-orm 0.45.2 and postgres 3.4.9 pinned in bun.lock), db.execute() resolves to a postgres.js Result object, which extends Array (node_modules/postgres/src/result.js:1) and is empty (length 0) for an UPDATE without RETURNING while carrying the affected-row count on .count. Drizzle's raw execute path returns the driver object unchanged (node_modules/drizzle-orm/postgres-js/session.js:30-33, 'return await client.unsafe(query, params)'). The array branch returns first, so the helper…
resolution: Fixed in #2983: `affectedRowCount` in `app/lib/worker/poll-jobs.server.ts` reads `count` first (postgres.js resolves `db.execute()` to an Array that carries it) and keeps the array length as the fallback for plain rows.
acceptanceCriteria: failJob should log worker.job.dead_letter and page on-call through notifyOps when a job permanently fails, resetStaleClaims should log worker.stale_claims_reset when it reclaims a row from a dead worker, deadLetterExhaustedJobs should log worker.exhausted_jobs_dead_lettered when it buries an exhausted row, and worker.claim_lost should be logged only when a post-claim write was actually rejected by the claim fence.

recommendedTitle: Workspace API keys keep their full scope set after the member who minted them is removed or demoted
summary: A workspace API key is a bearer credential whose authority comes exclusively from the `scopes` array on the key row
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. An API key's scopes are re-derived from its creator's current role on every request, so removing or demoting the creator narrows or revokes the key; a key with no recorded creator fails closed with the same 401.
rootCause: The API-key principal model records the creator (`created_by`) but never binds the key to a live workspace principal, and no cascade exists between a membership change and the key rows. `created_by` has no surviving foreign key (dropped in client/migrations/20260919120000_drop_legacy_auth_users_fks.sql:16) and is read by no runtime path; the scope ceiling `assertScopesWithinActorRole` (app/lib/platform-members.server.ts:120) is applied once at mint time against the creator's then-current role and, as the code comment at app/lib/platform-members.server.ts:80-89 states, is never re-derived. The session path re-resolves the role on every request (app/lib/capability-guard.server.ts:54,…
resolution: Fixed in #2928 (`13e1a6c4`): `app/lib/api-auth.server.ts:108-118` re-checks the creator's current role, with the ceiling in `app/lib/capabilities.ts` and the lookup in `app/lib/workspace-members-db.server.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: Removing or demoting a workspace member ends that member's effective authority over the workspace, including through credentials the member issued. The platform already implements that for sessions: the membership lookup in `requireWorkspaceAccess` / `getUserRole` yields 404 'Workspace not found' for a non-member, so the session dies with the membership. A key should either be bound to a live membership - with its capability set re-checked against the creator's current role - or be revoked automatically when that membership is removed or reduced. The platform's chosen compensations for key durability are admin-only minting, a mint-time role cap and mandatory expiry; a membership-driven cascade is the missing one. (Note: the platform does NOT fail closed on workspace suspension either - `workspace.disabled` is read only by cron fan-out, number-rental billing and the admin console - so the asymmetry is specifically between the session path and the API-key path on membership change.)

recommendedTitle: POST /api/jobs/twilio-open-sync stores unbounded sweep limits: a negative limit silently removes the sweep's LIMIT and a non-positive maxAgeMinutes collapses…
summary: POST /api/jobs/twilio-open-sync narrows callLimit, messageLimit and maxAgeMinutes with a bare `typeof body.X === "number"` check, and the job's params schema (legacyNumericParam) keeps any finite number, negative and zero included
currentBehavior: Fixed on dev. The Twilio open-sync cron route replaces a negative or zero sweep limit with its default instead of storing it, so a bad request cannot turn the bounded sweep into an unbounded read or collapse the 404 grace window. A stored bad value is clamped when the job is parsed, and the successor job inherits the defaults rather than the current job's parameters.
rootCause: The per-route body narrowing (app/routes/api+/jobs+/twilio-open-sync.action.server.ts:15) accepts any number and the registered params schema (app/lib/worker/job-params.server.ts:68 -> legacyNumericParam, app/lib/worker/job-registry.server.ts:124-132) has no lower bound, so an out-of-range value is stored as job.params and later used both as a SQL row bound and as a provider page size. withReschedule (app/lib/worker/handlers/cron.server.ts:91) then copies the parsed params verbatim into the chain successor, so whenever a workspace-less job carries such a value it becomes the chain's permanent configuration instead of one run's parameter.
resolution: Fixed in #2985: `sweepNumber` in `app/routes/api+/jobs+/twilio-open-sync.action.server.ts`, the clamp in `boundedSweepNumber` (`app/lib/worker/job-params.server.ts`), and the successor inheriting `TWILIO_OPEN_SYNC_DEFAULTS` (`app/lib/worker/handlers/cron.server.ts`).
acceptanceCriteria: The three numbers are the sweep's budgets, not free-form input: callLimit/messageLimit bound how many open rows one run may touch, and maxAgeMinutes is the grace window that decides when a call the provider does not know yet may be terminalized ('Terminalize it as failed once it is old enough that a race with call creation is impossible', app/lib/twilio-open-sync.server.ts:234). A limit must be a positive integer and maxAgeMinutes must be at least 1, so a negative or zero value can never be stored; and the chain successor must not inherit an unvalidated parameter, because the successor is the platform's only scheduler for this job ('These chains are the only scheduler: there is no pg_cron and no external trigger', app/lib/worker/handlers/shared.server.ts:8), so a bad value there is permanent.
